sources.source_date: public-act citation line ends P.A. 23-48, S. 1, 3

slice.from: Sec. 19a-535. (Formerly Sec. 19-616). Transfer or discharge of residents.

sources.notes: The standing packet (2026-08-30) recorded this source as unreachable to curl (certificate verification failure) and to the session HTTP fetch tool, and was captured through a browser instead, marked not re-verifiable by an automated pass. Retested 2026-09-08: plain curl with a browser user-agent now returns HTTP 200 with the real statute text (951 KB) -- the same transient-failure pattern already documented elsewhere in this portfolio for codeofarrules.arkansas.gov and cdph.ca.gov/dhcs.ca.gov. body scope pulls the whole chapter 368v page (all sections of the chapter); chap_368v.htm prints each section heading twice -- once in the chapter's table of contents, once over the section's own text -- so the slice takes the *second* occurrence of the section heading (from_occurrence: 2), per this project's standing rule to anchor on the body occurrence, not the table of contents. The 'to' anchor (the next section's heading, 19a-535a) is a superset of the original hand-cut boundary: it also picks up the section's own History annotation note and a cross-reference to Sec. 17b-454, which the standing packet's PENDING list says were captured in the browser but not carried into the packet -- this recipe closes that gap rather than reproducing the narrower cut.

sources.title: Connecticut General Statutes § 19a-537, Nursing home responsibilities re reservation of beds. Reimbursement. Readmission (chapter 368v)
sources.source_date: public-act citation line ends P.A. 22-58, S. 4
sources.notes: Same page, template and transport as source 1 -- chap_368v.htm prints every section heading twice (chapter table of contents, then the section's own text), so from_occurrence: 2 lands the slice in the body, per this project's standing rule. The 'to' anchor's default occurrence (1) is correct here because it counts within the tail *after* the from-match, per capture.py's apply_slice, and the chapter's table of contents (which holds the only other 'Sec. 19a-537a.' heading) sits before that point, not after. This is Connecticut's bed-hold and readmission statute: subsection (b) the reservation duty, (c) the 15-day self-pay hold, (d) the Medicaid reimbursement conditions (up to 7 days plus 8 additional, and 21 home-leave days), (e) the first-available-bed obligation once the hold period is exceeded, and (f)-(i) a second, separate hearing route for a refused readmission, distinct from section 19a-535's transfer/discharge hearing.

sources.title: Connecticut Department of Social Services — Office of Legal Counsel, Regulations and Administrative Hearings (OLCRAH), Contact
sources.notes: Plain curl, no user-agent needed (200 with no UA, tested 2026-09-17). This is the departmental page the statute's notice provision points to without naming: the mailing address ('DSS-OLCRAH, 55 Farmington Avenue, Hartford CT 06105'), the OLCRAH email (olcrah.DSS@ct.gov), and the Administrative Hearings telephone numbers. A companion page at the same host, .../requesting-a-hearing, states the filing mechanics (Hearing Request Form, or a signed letter) and the two clocks already quoted from the statute; only the Contact page's mailing address and email are quoted here to avoid restating the statute's own words as a second source's.
